issues.title: Empty first value of a singleton header counts as absent
issues.explanation: parsed[key] is a truthiness check, so 'Content-Length:' followed by 'Content-Length: 10' does not trigger the keep-first rule; the duplicate falls through and replaces the empty first value, unlike Node.
issues.fix: const hasKey = utils.hasOwnProp(parsed, key); if (!key || (hasKey && utils.hasOwnProp(ignoreDuplicateOf, key))) return;

issues.title: Empty first value dropped when joining duplicates
issues.explanation: Same truthiness test when merging: 'X-Foo:' then 'X-Foo: a' yields 'a' instead of ', a', losing the first (empty) occurrence.

issues.title: Inherited Object.prototype keys look like existing headers
issues.explanation: parsed and ignoreDuplicateOf are plain objects, so lookups see inherited properties: a header named constructor or toString is dropped on its first occurrence, and a polluted Object.prototype changes which headers are kept or merged. The fix switched every presence check (lines 53, 58, 64) to own-property checks.
issues.fix: Use utils.hasOwnProp(parsed, key) / utils.hasOwnProp(ignoreDuplicateOf, key) instead of property reads.
